h1: The 8 Best Outdoor Storage Sheds Under $1000 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Outdoor Storage Shed 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 outdoor storage sheds under $1000 scored on floor area, material, floor and door design, from 15 to 96 sq ft.
summary: The EASYHAWK 6x8 resin shed is the all-rounder: 48 square feet, a floor, a window and a lockable door. If you need real volume, the DAUSOLA 8x12 metal shed gives you 96 square feet. The Aoxun 7.3 by 5.3 steel shed adds a floor in a mid-size footprint, the two 6x4 resin sheds cover a mower and tools, and the 5x3 Patiowell is the small-patio pick.
intro: Most buyers pick a shed by the picture and the price, and then find out the floor is the thing they needed. A shed without a floor sits straight on whatever you built the base from, so every spill, every damp patch and every mouse has a clear path in. A floor, a flat base and a way to anchor the shed down matter more than a dozen features on the product page.

We ranked eight sheds under $1000 on the dimensions and materials in the listings: floor area in square feet, resin versus metal, whether a floor is included, and door and window design. Square footage here is worked out from the stated length and width, and we kept to what each listing says, because shed specs vary and a few of these listings are thin.

products.name: EASYHAWK 6x8 FT Resin Storage Shed with Floor, Window & Lockable Door
products.verdict: 48 square feet of resin shed with a floor, a window and a lockable door.
products.description:
EASYHAWK's 6 by 8 foot resin shed gives you 48 square feet of floor space, and it ships with a floor, a window and a lockable door. Resin does not rust and needs no painting, and the lock keeps mowers and tools from walking away.

It tops the ranking because it is the only shed here that lists all three features at once. The DAUSOLA is twice the size but states no floor or window, and the 7.3 by 5.3 Aoxun is smaller. The price puts it in the $500-plus bracket, the highest in this group, and still comfortably under $1000.

Buy it for a garden shed that holds a mower, a bike and tools. The caveat is that resin sheds need a level, solid base and anchoring in wind, so plan the foundation before the shed arrives.
products.idealFor: Homes that need a lockable shed for a mower and tools.
products.skipIf: You need more than 48 square feet of floor.

products.name: DAUSOLA 8x12 FT Outdoor Storage Shed, Metal Garden Tool Sheds for Backyard
products.verdict: A metal 8 by 12 foot shed with 96 square feet, the biggest footprint here.
products.description:
The DAUSOLA is a metal shed of 8 by 12 feet, which works out to 96 square feet. That is double the EASYHAWK and four times the small resin sheds, and it lands under $500.

Second place is earned because the listing does not mention a floor, a window or a lockable door, the features that put EASYHAWK ahead. A metal shed of this size is also more of a project: it is a larger base to prepare, and steel can dent and scratch more readily than resin. What you get is raw volume for the money.

A fit for a large yard with ride-on mowers, bikes and power tools. The caveat is the base: check for a floor or plan to build one, and confirm any local rules that apply to a shed of this size.
products.idealFor: Large yards storing mowers, bikes and tools.
products.skipIf: You want a floor and a window listed.

products.name: Aoxun 7.3'x5.3' Shed with Floor Galvanized Steel Outdoor Storage Shed Brown
products.verdict: Galvanized steel with a floor, in a mid-size footprint of about 39 square feet.
products.description:
Aoxun's 7.3 by 5.3 foot shed is made of galvanized steel and includes a floor, giving roughly 39 square feet of space in the $200 to $500 bracket. Galvanizing coats the steel in zinc, which slows rust and is the reason this material lasts outdoors.

It ranks third because the floor and steel are real upgrades over the smaller Aoxun sheds, but the footprint is well below the EASYHAWK's 48 square feet and the DAUSOLA's 96. The floor is the feature that separates it from the DAUSOLA on the page. Steel also handles sun and cold differently from resin: it will not warp but can dent.

Choose it for a patio or small yard. The caveat is that steel can get hot in summer, so do not store items that dislike heat.
products.idealFor: Small yards needing a steel shed with a floor.
products.skipIf: You want a window or a bigger footprint.

products.name: Patiowell 6x4 FT Resin Outdoor Storage Shed with Floor, Light Gray
products.verdict: Resin walls, an included floor and a light gray finish across 24 square feet.
products.description:
Patiowell builds its 6 by 4 foot shed from resin and includes a floor, which gives 24 square feet and costs $200 to $500. The light gray finish reflects more sun than dark panels, which keeps the interior cooler.

It ranks fourth because it is a small shed priced like a mid-size one. The Gizoon adds 0.4 feet of depth for similar money, and the Aoxun steel shed is bigger at the same bracket. What keeps the Patiowell here is the floor and the resin build, which cover the basics for a lawn mower and hand tools.

A fit for a narrow side yard. The caveat is the size: 24 square feet fills fast, and a ride-on mower will not fit.
products.idealFor: Narrow side yards holding a mower and hand tools.
products.skipIf: You own a ride-on mower or bulky equipment.

products.name: Gizoon 6x4.4 FT Resin Storage Shed with Floor, Outdoor Plastic Shed, Grey
products.verdict: A grey resin shed with a floor and 6 by 4.4 feet of space, about 26 square feet.
products.description:
Gizoon's resin shed measures 6 by 4.4 feet, about 26 square feet, with a floor included, in the $200 to $500 bracket. The extra 0.4 feet of depth over the Patiowell is small but useful for long-handled tools.

It ranks fifth because the gain over the Patiowell is marginal, and the Patiowell lists its finish and resin more clearly. The listing otherwise gives little: no window, lock or venting is mentioned. Against the larger EASYHAWK, it lacks the lock and window and holds roughly half the volume.

Good for a small garden that needs a tidy place for tools. The caveat is the thin listing, so confirm the door latch and ventilation before you buy.
products.idealFor: Small gardens needing a tidy tool store.
products.skipIf: You need a lock or a window listed.

products.name: Aoxun 4×6 FT All-Weather Resin Storage Shed, Dark Gray
products.verdict: Dark gray all-weather resin on a compact 24 square foot footprint.
products.description:
Aoxun sells this 4 by 6 foot model as dark gray, all-weather resin, which gives 24 square feet for $200 to $500. The all-weather label points to resin that stays stable in sun and rain.

It ranks sixth because the listing does not mention a floor, which the Patiowell and Gizoon do. For the same footprint, that omission matters, since a shed without a floor is only as dry as the base beneath it. Dark gray also absorbs more heat than light gray, so the interior will run warmer on sunny days.

A choice for a small yard on a prepared slab. The caveat is that without a stated floor you should plan a solid base and check the listing before purchase.
products.idealFor: Small yards with a prepared slab.
products.skipIf: You want the floor included in the box.

products.name: Aoxun 6.2x4 FT Shed Outdoor Storage Shed, Brown
products.verdict: A brown 6.2 by 4 foot shed of about 25 square feet in the $100 to $200 bracket.
products.description:
Aoxun's 6.2 by 4 foot shed offers about 25 square feet in brown, in the $100 to $200 bracket, the lower of the two price tiers in this ranking. The listing gives no material, floor or door details.

It ranks seventh because the missing specs make it hard to rank higher. The Patiowell and Gizoon share a similar footprint and say they include a floor and resin, and they sit in the next price bracket up. The saving here is real, but you are buying with less information.

Buy it if the price is the priority and you can verify the material and floor on the listing. The caveat is that without those details you are taking a risk on durability.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who will verify the details first.
products.skipIf: You want clear specs before buying.

products.name: Patiowell 5x3 FT Outdoor Storage Shed, Brown
products.verdict: The smallest shed here at 5 by 3 feet, 15 square feet, in the $100 to $200 bracket.
products.description:
Patiowell's 5 by 3 foot shed is the smallest in the ranking at 15 square feet, in brown, in the $100 to $200 bracket. It is the one that fits on a balcony, a narrow patio or beside a back door.

It ranks last because 15 square feet holds little: a few tools, a hose and some pots. The listing gives no material or floor information. Against the 6 by 4 sheds, it saves space and money but gives up nearly 40 percent of the floor area, which you will feel as soon as you add a wheelbarrow.

Choose it for a tight outdoor spot where anything bigger will not fit. The caveat is capacity, so measure what you need to store before ordering.
products.idealFor: Balconies and small patios needing a compact box.
products.skipIf: You store a mower, wheelbarrow or large tools.

whatMatters.factor: Floor area, not the headline size
whatMatters.detail: A shed called 6x8 has 48 square feet, but the usable space is less once walls and shelves go in. Multiply length by width to compare. Match the area to what you store: a push mower needs far less than a ride-on. Measure your largest item before you pick a size.

Resin does not rust and needs no paint, but can flex in high wind and fade over years. Galvanized steel is stiffer and resists rust through its zinc coating, but can dent and gets hot inside. Check the material in the title or specs, and be wary of listings that name neither.

A built-in floor keeps the interior off damp ground and away from pests. Without one, the shed is only as good as the base you build. Look for with floor in the title, as on the EASYHAWK and Patiowell, and plan a level base either way.

A shed is a large sail in the wind, and an unanchored one can shift or lift. A flat, firm base of gravel, pavers or a slab keeps it square and dry. Check the listing for anchoring options, and confirm any local rules for sheds of a given size.

A lockable door protects tools and a window lets in daylight so you are not rummaging in the dark. These features are listed on the EASYHAWK and absent on most others. Look for lockable and window in the title, and ask whether a padlock hasp is included.

faq.q: Do these sheds need a foundation?
faq.a: Yes. Every shed, including the EASYHAWK and the DAUSOLA, needs a level, firm base such as gravel, pavers or a slab. Without one, the walls twist, the door sticks and water pools underneath. Prepare the base before delivery.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing by price and skipping the floor question. The Aoxun 4x6 and 6.2x4 do not state a floor, while the Patiowell 6x4 and Gizoon do. A missing floor means building your own, and that cost belongs in the budget.

faq.q: Is the EASYHAWK worth it over the DAUSOLA?
faq.a: If you want a lock, a window and a floor, yes. The EASYHAWK offers 48 square feet with all three. The DAUSOLA gives 96 square feet for less, but states none of them, so you may add them yourself.

faq.q: Can I put the shed together alone?
faq.a: Small sheds like the Patiowell 5x3 are manageable for one person, but the 8x12 DAUSOLA and 6x8 EASYHAWK need a helper because panels are large and awkward. Assemble on a calm day, as flat panels catch wind.

faq.q: How do I look after a resin or steel shed?
faq.a: Wash resin walls with mild soap and clear the roof of leaves. On the galvanized Aoxun 7.3 by 5.3, touch up any scratches before rust starts. Check the door and fasteners each season, and keep gutters from overflowing onto the base.

It depends on your area and the size of the shed. Larger footprints like the DAUSOLA 8x12 are more likely to trigger rules on size, setbacks or foundations than a 5x3 Patiowell. Check with your local building office before you buy.

finalTake: The EASYHAWK 6x8 is the shed to buy for most yards: a floor, a window and a lockable door in 48 square feet. Choose the DAUSOLA 8x12 when you need real volume, and the Aoxun 7.3 by 5.3 steel shed for a mid-size space with a floor. Whatever you pick, spend the first weekend on the base and anchoring, because that decides how long it lasts.
